# Reviewer minutes per page, with and without proposals

| Arm | Seconds per page | Minutes per page | Pages per hour | Pages | Documents |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| proposals | 67s per page (61 to 73), 10 pages over 10 documents | 1.1 | 54 | 10 | 10 |
| unaided | 130s per page (103 to 159), 10 pages over 10 documents | 2.2 | 28 | 10 | 10 |

The proposals arm is **1.9 times** the speed of the unaided arm on this evidence.

Intervals are 95 percent bootstrap percentile intervals resampled over documents rather than pages, because pages within a record are not independent: one record's density of third parties, and one reviewer's growing familiarity with its template, are single facts and not many.

The unaided arm is served the same records with the proposals dropped before the session is built, so the reviewer finds and categorises every severance themselves. Highlighting the spans and hiding only the suggested category would measure how long it takes to agree with a highlight, which is not the question.

## How right each arm was

Against the corpus labels, which are known by construction. A must-redact span is leaked unless every letter and digit of it was withheld; a must-keep span is over-redacted if any of it was.

| What was released | Leak rate | Over-redaction rate | Unlabelled text withheld, characters per page | Pages |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| reviewer, with proposals | 2.6% (0.0% to 6.0%), n=76 | 5.4% (0.0% to 14.0%), n=185 | 0 | 10 |
| reviewer, unaided | 1.5% (0.0% to 5.3%), n=65 | 5.2% (0.0% to 13.4%), n=193 | 2 | 10 |
| the tool's proposals, nobody reviewing, same records | 3.5% (1.2% to 6.3%), n=141 | 24.1% (19.3% to 28.5%), n=378 | 0 | 20 |

The fourth column is text withheld outside every labelled span, such as the word "sibling" beside a severed name. The labels cannot say whether withholding it was right, so it is in neither rate; it is counted because it costs the reviewer time and the requester text, and would otherwise appear nowhere.

## Record by record

No record has yet been reviewed in both arms, by two different reviewers, so there is no paired comparison. It needs at least two reviewers.

## Each reviewer

| Reviewer | Minutes per page, with proposals | Minutes per page, unaided | Pages |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| reviewer-1 | 1.1 | 2.2 | 20 |

Each reviewer did half the records with proposals and the other half unaided, never the same record twice, and the halves and their order swap between reviewers. The first page of each arm is practice and is in none of these numbers.
